# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a Geometry Dash–style browser game containing 5 levels, 10 selectable cube skins, and 10 achievements.

## Requirements
- User request: "Geometry dash, 5 levels, 10 cubes, 10 achievements"
- Responsive browser game, polished neon visual style, playable on desktop and mobile.

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS static site (no package manager); canvas game rendered on a fixed logical playfield with responsive scaling.
- 5 handcrafted levels with spikes, blocks, saws, pads, orbs, shards, gravity portals, speed portals.
- 10 cube skins with unlock conditions; 10 achievements tracked in localStorage.
- Procedural WebAudio music/SFX, no external audio assets.
- Shards: 3 per level (15 total) as optional collectibles.
- Added `window.__gd` debug hook for warp/freeze/state verification; intended to be removed before final delivery.
- Auto-player Node simulator used to prove all levels beatable.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core engine, level data, cube/achievement data, skin renderer, audio engine, main game loop/UI, styling, favicon, README not yet updated.
- All 5 levels verified beatable by `node tools/simulate.mjs` (100% by auto-player).
- Verified menu, level select, cube wardrobe, achievements, gameplay, jump, death/auto-respawn, pause, results overlays in headed Chromium.
- Fixed major rendering bug: world objects were not camera-translated; added `ctx.translate(-camX, 0)` in `drawWorldObjects`.
- Fixed player/particles being offset twice by `view.offsetY`.
- Improved block/spike rendering contrast.
- Removed preview text and difficulty dots that truncated level names; added 5-column desktop level grid.
- Added mobile portrait scaling (logical width ~620, larger cube, floor at 72% screen height) and hid jump hint in portrait.
- Verified mobile portrait menu/game and mobile level select; verified landscape menu/game.

### Active
- Final visual polish and cleanup.
- Last screenshots showed landscape gameplay and menu looking good, but the landscape menu screen was captured while a level was still running behind it (HUD visible through overlay); not a real menu state.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining visual polish: add a filled neon sun disc, make death explosion/burst punchier, potentially strengthen HUD shard icons.
2. Re-test speed portal visuals in level 5 and gravity cube orientation.
3. Remove `window.__gd` debug hook and any debug-only code (`debugFreeze` checks), or confirm acceptable to keep.
4. Clear test localStorage / restart browser to verify fresh-save state (0/5, 0/15, 0/10).
5. Take final screenshots at desktop, portrait mobile, landscape mobile.
6. Update `README.md` with game description, controls, features, and how to run.
7. Run `node tools/simulate.mjs` and `node --check` again after edits.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: app shell, all screens, HUD, overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full neon design system, responsive layouts, mobile/landscape rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: game loop, rendering, input, UI wiring, save/evaluation, debug hook.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine.js`: shared physics/collision, player state, threat finder.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/levels.js`: 5 level definitions, object builders, themes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data.js`: 10 cubes, 10 achievements, stats computation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/skins.js`: canvas cube skin rendering, previews.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: procedural music/SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tools/simulate.mjs`: headless bot that validates all 5 levels.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/favicon.svg`: game favicon.

## Important Context
- Dev server: tmux session `gd`, `PORT=3002 RUNTIME_DIR=$RUNTIME_DIR ./start.sh`, log `/tmp/opencode/gd-server.log`, URL `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser viewport currently resized to `844x390`; use `playwright-cli resize` as needed.
- Screenshots saved to `screenshots/` (gitignored); `playwright-cli` browser session is open.
- `window.__gd` API currently supports `start(id)`, `state()`, `freeze(bool)`, `warp(pct,{ceiling})`, `jump()`, `collection()`, `objects()`.
- localStorage key: `geometry-dash-neon-v1`; test browser has debug-earned progress (1/5, 2 shards? displays 0/15 shards, 2/10 cubes, 2/10 awards), so clear it before final fresh screenshots.

- Known minor issue: mobile `hud-hint` hidden in portrait via CSS; hint fade animation may not restart across level starts.
- `screenshots/` and all runtime/server files are gitignored; game source files are uncommitted and not yet pushed.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

# Geometry Dash — Neon Edition

A complete, dependency-free Geometry Dash–style rhythm platformer for the browser. Five handcrafted levels, ten cube skins and ten achievements — all rendered on a neon canvas with procedurally generated music and sound effects.

## Play

The game is a static site. From this directory, serve it over HTTP (ES modules do not run from `file://`):

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000
```

Then open <http://localhost:3000>. Any static file server works; no build step or package install is required.

## Controls

| Action | Desktop | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jump | `Space`, `W`, `↑` or click | Tap anywhere |
| Auto-jump | Hold the jump input | Hold a finger down |
| Pause / resume | `Esc` | Pause button |

The game scales to the viewport, supports portrait and landscape phones, and keeps the playfield inside safe-area insets.

## Features

- **5 levels** — Stereo Dawn, Neon Rush, Circuit Breaker, Gravity Well and Final Overdrive. Each has its own palette, soundtrack tempo and obstacle pattern.
- **Hazards and gadgets** — spikes, blocks, saw blades, jump pads, jump orbs, gravity portals, speed portals and a finish gate.
- **10 cube skins** — unlockable through level clears, shard collection, jumps, deaths and total completion. The selected cube is rendered in-game and in the wardrobe preview.
- **10 achievements** — progression, skill, collection and persistence milestones, with toast notifications.
- **15 shards** — three optional collectibles per level, tracked per save.
- **Per-level stats** — best percentage, attempts, completed flag and collected shards persist in `localStorage`.
- **Procedural audio** — WebAudio synthesizes the music and all jump, shard, portal, death and victory sounds. No audio files to download.
- **Instant retry** — death triggers a short explosion and automatically restarts the attempt.
- **Responsive UI** — menus, level select, wardrobe, achievements, pause screen and results overlay all adapt to desktop and mobile.

## Project layout

```text
index.html          App shell, screens, HUD and overlays
styles.css          Neon design system and responsive layouts
js/main.js          Game loop, rendering, input, UI and save logic
js/engine.js        Physics, collision and player state
js/levels.js        Level definitions, object builders and themes
js/data.js          Cube, achievement and stat definitions
js/skins.js         Canvas cube rendering and previews
js/audio.js         Procedural WebAudio music and SFX
favicon.svg         Neon app icon
tools/simulate.mjs  Headless bot that verifies every level is beatable
```

## Verification

Check JavaScript syntax and run the headless level bot:

```bash
for f in js/*.js; do node --check "$f"; done
node tools/simulate.mjs
```

The simulator plays all five levels start to finish and confirms a 100% clear on each.

## Save data

Progress is stored under the `geometry-dash-neon-v1` key in `localStorage`. Clearing site data resets levels, shards, cubes, achievements and statistics.

20: # Geometry Dash — Neon Edition
21: 
22: A complete, dependency-free Geometry Dash–style rhythm platformer for the browser. Five handcrafted levels, ten cube skins and ten achievements — all rendered on a neon canvas with procedurally generated music and sound effects.
23: 
24: ## Play
25: 
26: The game is a static site. From this directory, serve it over HTTP (ES modules do not run from `file://`):
27: 
28: ```bash
29: python3 -m http.server 3000
30: ```
31: 
32: Then open <http://localhost:3000>. Any static file server works; no build step or package install is required.
33: 
34: ## Controls
35: 
36: | Action | Desktop | Touch |
37: | --- | --- | --- |
38: | Jump | `Space`, `W`, `↑` or click | Tap anywhere |
39: | Auto-jump | Hold the jump input | Hold a finger down |
40: | Pause / resume | `Esc` | Pause button |
41: 
42: The game scales to the viewport, supports portrait and landscape phones, and keeps the playfield inside safe-area insets.
43: 
44: ## Features
45: 
46: - **5 levels** — Stereo Dawn, Neon Rush, Circuit Breaker, Gravity Well and Final Overdrive. Each has its own palette, soundtrack tempo and obstacle pattern.
47: - **Hazards and gadgets** — spikes, blocks, saw blades, jump pads, jump orbs, gravity portals, speed portals and a finish gate.
48: - **10 cube skins** — unlockable through level clears, shard collection, jumps, deaths and total completion. The selected cube is rendered in-game and in the wardrobe preview.
49: - **10 achievements** — progression, skill, collection and persistence milestones, with toast notifications.
50: - **15 shards** — three optional collectibles per level, tracked per save.
51: - **Per-level stats** — best percentage, attempts, completed flag and collected shards persist in `localStorage`.
52: - **Procedural audio** — WebAudio synthesizes the music and all jump, shard, portal, death and victory sounds. No audio files to download.
53: - **Instant retry** — death triggers a short explosion and automatically restarts the attempt.
54: - **Responsive UI** — menus, level select, wardrobe, achievements, pause screen and results overlay all adapt to desktop and mobile.
55: 
56: ## Project layout
57: 
58: ```text
59: index.html          App shell, screens, HUD and overlays
60: styles.css          Neon design system and responsive layouts
61: js/main.js          Game loop, rendering, input, UI and save logic
62: js/engine.js        Physics, collision and player state
63: js/levels.js        Level definitions, object builders and themes
64: js/data.js          Cube, achievement and stat definitions
65: js/skins.js         Canvas cube rendering and previews
66: js/audio.js         Procedural WebAudio music and SFX
67: favicon.svg         Neon app icon
68: tools/simulate.mjs  Headless bot that verifies every level is beatable
69: ```
70: 
71: ## Verification
72: 
73: Check JavaScript syntax and run the headless level bot:
74: 
75: ```bash
76: for f in js/*.js; do node --check "$f"; done
77: node tools/simulate.mjs
78: ```
79: 
80: The simulator plays all five levels start to finish, confirms a 100% clear on each, and collects all 15 shards along the way.
81: 
82: ## Save data
83: 
84: Progress is stored under the `geometry-dash-neon-v1` key in `localStorage`. Clearing site data resets levels, shards, cubes, achievements and statistics.

## Objective
- Build a Geometry Dash–style browser game, now adding the **Time Machines**, **Ystep** and **Clutterfunk** levels plus a functional in-game **level editor**.

## Requirements
- Original user request: "Geometry dash, 5 levels, 10 cubes, 10 achievements"
- New user request: "please add Time Machines, Ystep and clutterfunk levels and please add a level editor."
- Responsive browser game, polished neon visual style, playable on desktop and mobile.

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS static site; canvas gameplay rendered on a fixed logical playfield with responsive scaling.
- Keep original 5 levels, append 3 new levels: `l6` Time Machines, `l7` Ystep, `l8` Clutterfunk.
- Keep 10 cubes and 10 achievements; update all-level / all-shard achievements dynamically to 8 levels and 24 shards.
- Editor design: full-screen canvas-backed editor, single saved custom level, grid-snapped placement, tool palette, pan/undo/clear/save/test playtest.
- Editor will use `localStorage` key `geometry-dash-neon-editor-v1`.
- Playtest uses a custom-level flag so editor testing does not affect normal save stats/achievements.
- Keep webfont/asset-free procedural audio and visuals.

## Work State
### Completed
- Original game fully built and verified: engine, 5 levels, 10 cubes, 10 achievements, 15 shards, menus, HUD, audio, results, pause, responsive/mobile layouts.
- Removed shipping debug hook (`window.__gd`), tightened hint animation restart, improved sun disc and HUD shard icons.
- Fixed gravity portals to full height (`C` → `F-C`), allowing correct gravity restore; auto-player now collects all shards.
- Fixed level-select truncation at 844px and 568px widths; 3-column narrow-landscape layout.
- Added new levels `l6`–`l8` in `js/levels.js`; all 8 levels currently pass simulator at 100% with 3/3 shards:
  - `l6 Time Machines`, `l7 Ystep`, `l8 Clutterfunk`.
- Added 3 themes (`time`, `ystep`, `clutter`) and extended difficulty labels/colors to 8.
- Updated `js/data.js` dynamically: Legend = 8 levels, Completionist = 24 shards, Overdrive cube = all 8 levels.
- Updated simulator content check to 8 levels / 10 cubes / 10 achievements / 24 shards.
- Updated menu HTML: tagline, `8 LEVELS`, counts `0/8`, `0/24`, added `EDITOR` button, `levels-done` `0/8 COMPLETE`.
- Main.js imports `THEMES`, defines `LEVEL_COUNT`, `SHARD_TOTAL`, updated dynamic counts/result/HUD shard labels.
- README updated for original game; needs further update for 8 levels/editor.

### Active
- Implementing level editor UI and logic.
- Still need to add editor screen markup/CSS and JS state/render/input/save/playtest.
- Need final visual and functional browser verification for new levels, 8-card level grid, editor desktop/mobile.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add `#screen-editor` markup to `index.html`: top bar (back/name/save/test), tool palette, theme/speed controls, undo/clear, status footer.
2. Add editor CSS: overlay layer with pointer events passing through to canvas, desktop left/right panels, mobile bottom dock.
3. Implement editor state in `js/main.js`: load/sanitize/save `localStorage`, tools (`spike`, `block`, `saw`, `pad`, `orb`, `gravity`, `speed`, `shard`, `erase`), grid snapping, camera pan, pointer placement, delete, undo, clear.
4. Add `renderEditor(t)` using existing draw helpers; ghost preview, start/finish markers, ruler/grid.
5. Add editor menu action, keyboard shortcuts (`Esc`, arrows/A-D, Delete, Ctrl+Z), wheel scrolling.
6. Implement custom playtest flow: `buildEditorLevel()`, `customPlaytest` guards in `spawnPlayer`, `onDeath`, `onFinish`, shard handling, `quitToLevels`; return to editor after completion.
7. Update `README.md` for 8 levels, 24 shards, and editor usage.
8. Run `node tools/simulate.mjs`, `node --check js/*.js`, browser-test all 8 levels, editor placement/save/reload/playtest, and screenshots at desktop/portrait/landscape.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/levels.js`: 8 level definitions, themes, difficulty arrays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: game loop, rendering, input, save, must integrate editor + custom playtest.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: needs editor screen markup plus updated menu.
